ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The coil with the number of turns \( N = 1000 \), area \( S = 20 \, \mathrm{cm}^{2} \), and resistance \( r = 1 \, \Omega \) is placed horizontally. A uniform magnetic field \( B_{1} \) passes vertically downward through the coil, and its magnetic induction intensity \( B_{1} \) varies according to the pattern shown in the figure. The two ends of the coil are connected to two identical metal springs with a stiffness coefficient \( k = 100 \, \mathrm{N/m} \) and resistance \( R = 1.5 \, \Omega \). The upper ends of the two metal springs are fixed to the horizontal ceiling, and the lower ends suspend a horizontal metal rod. Another horizontal uniform magnetic field \( B_{2} \) is distributed perpendicular to the metal rod (as shown in the figure), with a magnetic field width of \( L = 10 \, \mathrm{cm} \). After closing the switch, the lengths of both springs change by \( \Delta x = 0.5 \, \mathrm{cm} \). The resistance of the wires and the metal rod is negligible.

1. What is the magnitude of the current through the metal rod after closing the switch?
2. What is the magnitude of the magnetic induction $B_{2}$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image on the left is a B1-t graph, with the vertical axis labeled B1/T and the horizontal axis labeled t/s; the straight line rises linearly from about 1 T at t=0; the dashed lines in the figure indicate that B1=3 T at t=0.4 s. The image on the right shows a horizontal coil in vertically downward B1; the coil is connected through a switch to two identical vertical metal springs; a horizontal metal rod is suspended from the lower ends of the springs, and the metal rod passes through a horizontal magnetic field B2 region represented by a dot array, with the width of the magnetic field labeled L. Reasoning: Unit conversion: S=20 cm^2=2.0×10^-3 m^2, L=10 cm=0.10 m, Δx=0.5 cm=0.005 m. From the slope of the graph, dB1/dt=(3-1)/0.4=5 T/s. The magnitude of the induced electromotive force produced by the coil is ε=N S dB1/dt=1000×2.0×10^-3×5=10 V. According to the connection method given in the problem, the coil resistance r and the resistance 2R of the two springs are connected in series, and the total resistance is r+2R=1+2×1.5=4 Ω, so the current through the metal rod is I=ε/(r+2R)=10/4=2.5 A. The metal rod is subjected to an Ampere force F=B2 I L in B2; the lengths of both springs change by Δx, corresponding to a total change in elastic force of 2kΔx=2×100×0.005=1 N. At equilibrium, B2 I L=2kΔx, therefore B2=1/(2.5×0.10)=4 T.
